name: List of Dirty, Naughty, Obscene and Otherwise Bad Words
mergedIntoNote: This source claims no path, and that is the whole design. It is a screen rather than
data: its only trace in the corpus is a Bloom filter inside the surname model, which is
attributed to the Census list it was trained on. `decoy-validate` would otherwise report
a source paying for nothing, which here would be a warning that can never be resolved.
note: Not corpus data. Nothing in this list is ever drawn, emitted or shipped as a value --
it is a screen, and the only thing that reaches the binary is a Bloom filter of hashed
substrings. That is deliberate twice over: it keeps the list out of a binary that people
grep and that security scanners read, and it keeps a slur out of the arena where a bug
in path resolution could surface one.
A generative model needs this. An n-gram over English characters will eventually walk
into something unfortunate, and 'it is statistically unlikely' is not a thing to tell
someone who found it in their staging database.
Pinned to a commit rather than a branch: `master` is the default ref and this list gets
edits, so a branch pin would silently change what the screen blocks.
One file per language, which is why this source rather than a hand-typed list -- the
screen has to grow with the models, and English is only the first.
